sentences.text: This civil application is moved for the purpose of stay of impugned order passed by Principal District Judge, Jalna on 30/06/2022 under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act (for short the 'Act') whereby the arbitral award passed by the Divisional Commissioner 63.ca6401.24.odt 1 of 5 in connection with acquisition of land for Samruddhi Express way is set aside.
2. The effect of the setting aside of the said order has resulted into initiation of fresh proceeding of arbitration by the Divisional Commissioner to redetermine the amount of compensation.

The appellant has raised objection to the impugned order passed by the learned Principal District Judge,

1 Jalna on the ground that the said Court has exceeded the jurisdiction as contemplated under Section 34 of the Act while causing interference in the impugned award.

sentences.text: 3. According to the learned counsel for the appellant the learned Principal District Judge, Jalna has considered the proceedings before it as if he is dealing with an appeal against the order passed by the Divisional Commissioner.

It is submitted that there is practically re-appreciation of evidence for the purpose of arriving at different findings than the one recorded by the Divisional Commissioner while passing award, which is not permissible in law.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has grievance about the present appeal being taken up for passing interim relief on the ground that request made by the learned counsel for the appellant for circulation was rejected earlier.

In this regard at this stage only it needs 63.ca6401.24.odt 2 of 5 to be recorded that though such circulation was refused, later on the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has pointed out the order passed by this Court in Writ Petition No.
15709/2023 wherein it is recorded that the hearing of the said petition would not be postponed unless there is a stay in appeal filed by the petitioner therein in the present appeal.
Thus, this Court finds no sound reason for not taking up this appeal for passing interim relief.

5. At this stage though this Court is not going into the merits of the case in detail, however, suffice is to say that the Court is expected to prima facie consider whether the impugned order passed by the learned Principal District Judge, Jalna is within the parameters of the scope of Section 34 of the Act.
6. It is sought to be argued on behalf of the learned counsel for the respondent that the judgments cited before the Divisional Commissioner which were relevant were ignored while passing the award.

It is also submitted that other aspects such as the improper determination of the amount of compensation contrary to the law settled by the Supreme Court has been taken into consideration by the learned Principal District Judge, Jalna.
It is also submitted that the N.A. Cess charged to the petitioner also indicates about there being use of the land as for the non agricultural purpose.
At this prima facie stage the order impugned is required to be tested to the touch stone of provision of Section 34 of the Act and scope of interference in an arbitral award.

Perusal of the said order prima facie indicates that the learned Principal District Judge, Jalna while causing interference in the impugned award passed by the Divisional Commissioner has merely relied upon the factum that the condition of the NA order was not required to be complied with.

In fact it is observed that under the Land Reference Code what constitute commencement of NA if some positive action taken by the applicant for obtaining NA permission such as developing or reclaiming the land etc.
It is thus observed that by doing so the character of the land is changed and it has become unfit for cultivation.
It is however clear from perusal of record that N.A. permission is conditional and it was granted for Industrial use (agro based).
Thus, order passed by learned District Judge deserves close and detail scrutiny.

Thus, at prima facie stage this Court finds it difficult to hold that no arguable case is made out by the appellant in order to challenge the order Maharashtra State Road Development ... vs Shaikh Nawab Shaikh Gulab And Ors on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149583722/
2 impugned.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Though grievance is made in respect of non continuation of the proceedings of arbitration before the Divisional Commissioner afresh, however, in this regard with material to note that any amount of compensation that the respondent would be entitled to can be directed to 63.ca6401.24.odt 4 of 5 be paid along with appropriate interest in accordance with the provisions of law.
As such no prejudice or irreparable loss will be caused to the respondent if the said proceedings do not continue for some time.

On the other hand if the impugned order is not stayed and if the arbitrator is permitted to decide the arbitration proceedings afresh for determination of compensation, it will only add to the complications to the issues.

Having regard to the afore stated facts, the appellant had made out a case for stay of the impugned order passed by the learned Principal District Judge, Jalna in Civil M.A. No. 158/2019.
9.

However, keeping in mind right of respondent to seek compensation for compulsory acquisition,
the Arbitration Appeal as well as Writ Petition stands expedited.
By consent of both sides these proceedings would be heard and decided together.
10. Stand over to 6th August, 2024.
(R. M. JOSHI, J.) ssp 63.ca6401.24.odt 5 of 5
